name: Lake Hartwell
type: Clear highland lake with standing timber; blueback herring
pool: Full pool 660 ft; a few feet lower in winter

stripers.doing: Big stripers cruise very shallow, often about 5 ft, in creeks and ditches and anywhere shallow with bait.
how: Herring cast or fished very shallow.
Live herring trolled shallow on planer boards.

spots.doing: Ditches from about 25 to 65 ft, channel swings and roadbeds. Rocky roadbeds or ones with brush hold the most fish. Late January, fish start moving toward pre-spawn staging areas along roadbeds.
how: Find big bait balls in ditches and stay mobile.
1/2 oz jigging spoon, blade bait, Damiki rig, Carolina rig, jig, drop shot.

crappie.doing: Crappie hold deep, 15 to 30 ft, on deep docks, brush, bridge pilings and creek channels near the mouths of major creeks.
how: Shoot a jig under deep docks and let it fall until it stops.
Small spoon or minnow worked slowly over brush.
Minnows trolled slowly along creek channels.

stripers.doing: Stripers push up the rivers and creeks with the herring as the water warms through the 50s. The upper lake and river channels hold the most fish.
how: Herring or gizzard shad about 40 ft behind the boards.
Unweighted bait 60 to 120 ft back on slow days.
Creek backs on warm afternoons; points and clay banks are steadier.

spots.doing: Spots move up rocky and clay points toward spawning pockets. They hold on the sides of long points and on rock piles from 5 to 30 ft.
how: A 1/4 oz ball-head swimbait crawled across rocky points.
Ned rig, shaky head or drop shot on the sides of long points.
Jerkbait on windy points and riprap.
Skip points with mushy bottoms; pea gravel and chunk rock hold fish.

crappie.doing: Crappie move from creek mouths toward the middle and backs of creeks onto stumps, laydowns, fish attractors and creek ledges.
how: Longline or spider-rig jigs and minnows through creek channels.
Minnow under a float on laydowns and brush.
Warm afternoons after a few warm days in a row.

stripers.doing: Herring move into pre-spawn staging areas up the creeks and stripers school on top for the first couple of hours after sunrise, longer on cloudy mornings. Then 25 to 35 ft on downlines nearby. Many fish run the main rivers.
how: Downline bluebacks at 25 to 35 ft in the same area.
Freelined herring on main points, shoals and ambush spots.

spots.doing: Bass are on beds all month in 1 to 4 ft around the full moon: bank and secondary points, laydowns, riprap and flooded bushes. Later in the month the shad and herring spawn on points.
how: 1/8 oz shaky head on laydowns and riprap; sight fish the big ones.
Wake bait and Fluke on points.

crappie.doing: Wide-open fishing with spawners in the backs of creeks in the big bays. Early near bottom in about 7 ft; by midday suspended 3 ft down over 6 ft.
how: Longline a double jig rig: 1/16 oz in front, 1/32 oz behind.
Pink-chartreuse early, then Junebug and chartreuse as the sun rises.

stripers.doing: The herring spawn on points, clay banks, riprap and marina walls at first light, and stripers crash them. By June they slide to brush on points in 15 to 35 ft, then deeper.
how: Walking bait, popper or wake bait on points and humps.
Herring pitched or freelined to points.
Downlines over brush in 15 to 35 ft.

spots.doing: Bass key on the herring and shad spawn on hard banks at dawn, then move to brush on points and humps as the water heads into the 80s.
how: Topwater or wake bait on clay points, bridges and marina walls.
Underspin, white spinnerbait or Fluke run along walls and riprap.
Drop shot or shaky head on brush in 15 to 25 ft.

crappie.doing: Crappie leave the banks for docks and brush in 10 to 15 ft. Singles and small groups are often the bigger fish.
how: Minnows set just above the brush.

stripers.doing: Late June to early July fish move deeper as the forage spawns out. Late July and August they go down-lake toward the dam: suspended at 30 to 40 ft over 40 to 50 ft, or 80 to 90 ft near the dam. Big fish hold in river channels over 100 ft, like the mouth of the Seneca.
how: 4 to 6 inch bluebacks; a 2 oz egg sinker in summer.
At 30 to 35 ft can outfish downlines.
Dam releases in the afternoon turn fish on in August.
Anchor over humps at 35 to 38 ft under lights in late summer.

spots.doing: Brush on points and humps at 15 to 30 ft. Follow bream and bait on the graph.
how: Pop-R or frog around the brush.
Drop shot in the same brush, very slowly.

crappie.doing: Crappie suspend over deep brush and under shaded docks, just above the thermocline. Night fishing under lights is good.
how: Minnows on a mini Carolina rig, set just above the brush.
Cast a small jig from 25 to 30 ft off the brush.
Lights on a deep dock or bridge.

stripers.doing: As the water cools, schools rise out of the depths and blow up on points and humps. Turnover kills the bite in creeks that have turned, so fish the clear water.
how: Run to surface schools and come in upwind.
Walking baits in calm water, swimbaits or a Magic Swimmer in wind; a spoon under marked fish.
Herring freelined about 100 ft back over humps and points.

spots.doing: As the water falls to the 50s and 60s, bass sit where 20 to 25 ft water ends, usually in ditches, plus rock piles and rock ridges.
how: Green-pumpkin Senko on a 1/4 oz jig head, or jig and pig dragged.
Fish Head Spin slowly, or a spoon dropped under bait balls.

crappie.doing: Crappie are on docks and brush early, then pull off cover into roaming schools in the creeks as the water cools.
how: Shoot jigs under docks with brush or shade.
Cast a jig just past a school and keep it above them.
Bright jigs in clear water, dark after rain.
